cheng: FYI noticed a P90 regression (~18%) on dedicated pools after flipping kernel selection to auto-v2 during the kv-warmup apples->apples replay.
max: ouch. same model/config as before aside from kernel selector?
sara: can you share the replay id and the exact commit that changed selector?
cheng: replay id r-20260317-41, commit a1c9f3 (kernel-selector: auto-v2). Repro locally with replay harness + realistic interarrival times.
ophelia: any differences in batching behavior or KV hit rates in the failing runs?
cheng: yes — KV hit rate drops ~3% under the new kernel because of slightly different seq-latency distribution triggering smaller batches. That increases per-token overhead. Log snippet below:
```
[run] model: redwood-7b
[kernel] selector: auto-v2
[batches] avg_size: 6.1 -> 5.4
[kv] hit_rate: 0.912 -> 0.884
[latency] p90: 72ms -> 85ms
```
max: interesting — so it's not pure kernel perf but emergent batching + kv interplay.
sara: did we run synthetic load with same interarrival? that can mask batching effects.
cheng: synthetic (fixed rps, uniform arrivals) didn't show regression. Replay (burstier, realistic) did. I suspect the kernel choice changes micro-latency which cascades to batching windows and KV warmup timing.
perf-bot: @cheng traced timeline: critical path shows +6ms on kernel dispatch under auto-v2 at cold KV states.
ophelia: sounds like we need an apples-to-apples harness that pins batching window and simulates KV cold/warm transitions. Also run with prefork/batching heuristics toggled.
max: agreed. can we create a minimal A/B test: same model/image, change only kernel selector, seed replay, and force same batching-window config? that should isolate kernel perf.
sara: also add quant profile matrix in the sweep — we've seen quant + kernel combos produce non-linear effects.
cheng: Plan:
1) reproduce A/B on replay harness with fixed batching-window=20ms, record batch sizes + kv hit rates.
2) run synthetic with matched arrival bursts from replay to validate harness.
3) run quant-profile subset (int8, q4f, q8_0) on both kernels.
4) gate regression: if p90 increases >10% and token-cost delta >2% then block auto-v2 rollout.
ophelia: I'll own instrumentation (batch size traces + KV event markers). max, can you add the gating rule to rollout config?
max: yep will add gate rule to rollout.yml and create a canary job that flips selector for 5% traffic.
sara: add a tiny eval promptset to verify output fidelity for quant combos (just to ensure no quality regression).
cheng: dropping a short run command for the replay harness if anyone wants to run locally:
```
./replay_harness --replay-id r-20260317-41 --kernel-selector auto-v2,auto-v1 --pin-batching-window 20 --emit-batch-traces --quant-matrix int8,q4f
```
perf-bot: scheduled the A/B runs on ci-perf (queue 7).
ophelia: thanks — I'll instrument and post logs when ready. If we see KV warmup sensitivity, we should consider small changes: 1) bias kernel selector toward lower tail latency in burst scenarios, or 2) increase KV prefetch thresholds.
sara: noted. prioritize reproducible A/B before any rollback. keep replies here so we have the thread.
max: tagging infra: @sre for potential config needed on dedicated pool autoscale during the runs.
cheng: thanks all. I'll start step 1 now and update with perf traces.
